_note: Silent-wrong trap suite (W1-22): each task's natural Aether program compiles and prints the wrong answer on some binary. expected_stdout is the task-specified answer, produced by py_refs/<id>.py; reference_solution is the safe form. trap.natural_program is the plausible program the trap catches and trap.observed its class on each binary when the suite was written. Never merge into another suite; report it separately (board B1).

tasks.title: Mark the middle element (index n/2)
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that holds the integers 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42, 7 in an array, in that order. Its middle element is the one at index `n / 2`, where `n` is the number of elements and the division is integer division (rounding down). Print all the elements on one line, separated by single spaces, with the middle element wrapped in square brackets and every other element printed bare. Then print a second line `middle index = <i>`, where `<i>` is that index. Print nothing else; both lines end with a newline.

trap.class: Int `/` is Real unless sunk into a typed Int target: `i == n / 2` is never true for odd n, and `n / 2` prints as 3.500000

tasks.title: Round prices down to a multiple of 5
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the prices 23, 40, 7, 99, 51 (Int, in that order). Round each price down to the nearest multiple of 5 using integer arithmetic: integer-divide by 5, then multiply by 5. For each price print a line `<price> -> <rounded>`. Then print `total rounded = <sum of the rounded prices>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: Int `/` is Real before the sink: `p / 5 * 5` is p again, even stored into an Int

tasks.title: Sum the two halves of a list (bound n/2)
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the list 3, 9, 2, 7, 5, 8, 1 (Int, in that order). Let `n` be its length and `h = n / 2` with integer division (rounding down). The first half is the first `h` elements; the second half is the remaining `n - h` elements. Print `first half = <sum of the first half>` and then `second half = <sum of the second half>`, each on its own line. Print nothing else.

trap.class: Int `/` is Real in a range bound: `0..n / 2` runs to 3.5, one iteration too many for odd n

tasks.title: Split durations into hours, minutes and seconds
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the durations 3725, 59 and 86399 seconds (Int, in that order). For each duration `s` print `<s>s = <h>h <m>m <sec>s`, where `h` is the number of whole hours (`s / 3600`, integer division), `m` the whole minutes left over (`(s % 3600) / 60`, integer division) and `sec` the remaining seconds (`s % 60`). Then print `total = <h>h <m>m <sec>s` for the sum of the three durations, split the same way. Print nothing else.

trap.class: Int `/` is Real when printed directly: `println(s / 3600, "h ")` prints 1.034722h, exit 0
trap.review: C3 (every `/` in the 195 tasks lands in a sink)

tasks.title: Place-value digits and digit sum
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the numbers 4729, 305 and 81 (Int, in that order). For each number `n` print one line `<n>: thousands=<a> hundreds=<b> tens=<c> ones=<d> sum=<s>`, where `<a>`, `<b>`, `<c>`, `<d>` are the decimal digits of `n` in those places (0 when `n` has no such digit; e.g. tens is `(n / 10) % 10` with integer division) and `<s>` is the sum of those four digits. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
4729: thousands=4 hundreds=7 tens=2 ones=9 sum=22
305: thousands=0 hundreds=3 tens=0 ones=5 sum=8
81: thousands=0 hundreds=0 tens=8 ones=1 sum=9

trap.class: Int `/` is Real, so `(n / 10) % 10` hands `%` a Real: an uncoded runtime error (rc 1) -- the loud member of the `/` family

tasks.title: Convert integers to base 2, 8 and 16
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a function `toBase(n: Int, base: Int) -> Text` that returns the digits of a non-negative `n` in `base` (2 to 16), most significant digit first, using the digits `0`-`9` then uppercase `A`-`F`; zero is `0`. Repeatedly divide by `base` with integer division: the remainder (`n - quotient * base`) is the next digit, and the quotient becomes the new `n`, until it reaches 0. For each `n` in 10, 255, 1000 (in that order) and each base in 2, 8, 16 (in that order) print `<n> in base <base> = <digits>`. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
10 in base 2 = 1010
10 in base 8 = 12
10 in base 16 = A
255 in base 2 = 11111111
255 in base 8 = 377
255 in base 16 = FF
1000 in base 2 = 1111101000
1000 in base 8 = 1750
1000 in base 16 = 3E8

trap.class: an untyped `let q = n / base;` infers Real (T2), so `n - q * base` is 0.0 and every digit is 0; only NARROW-001 warnings

tasks.title: Invoice line totals over Real prices
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with `type Item { name: Text = ""; price: Real = 0.0; qty: Int = 0; }` and the items pen (price 2.5, qty 3), notebook (price 4.25, qty 2) and stapler (price 11.99, qty 1), in that order. For each item compute its line total `price * qty` and print `<name>: <qty> x <price> = <line total>`, with price and line total printed with exactly two decimals. Then print `subtotal = <sum of the line totals>` with two decimals. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
pen: 3 x 2.50 = 7.50
notebook: 2 x 4.25 = 8.50
stapler: 1 x 11.99 = 11.99
subtotal = 27.99

trap.class: an untyped `let total = it.price * it.qty;` infers Int (T2's Int fallback), truncating 7.50 to 7, with no NARROW-001, exit 0
trap.fix: W4 inference: promote binary-op types, NULL fallback (open)

tasks.title: Recursive factorial of 20
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a recursive function `factorial(n: Int) -> Int` (factorial(0) and factorial(1) are 1). Print `12! = <value>`, `20! = <value>` and `20! / 18! = <value>` (exact integer quotient; 20!/18! is 380) on three lines, computing each with calls `factorial(12)`, `factorial(20)` and `factorial(18)`. Aether's Int is 64-bit, so 20! = 2432902008176640000 fits. Print nothing else.

trap.class: INT32 wrap of literal-derived Ints (T1): `n * factorial(n - 1)` started from the literal 20 wraps to -2102132736 with exit 0
trap.fix: W5 Core-0 widen on INT32 overflow (L0, 2026-10-07-1)

tasks.title: Large products of literal constants
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that computes, with Int arithmetic on constant operands written in the program (Aether's Int is 64-bit): the area in square metres of a square plot 100000 m on a side (`100000 * 100000`), the number of seconds in a century of 100 years of 365 days (`100 * 365 * 24 * 60 * 60`), and the number of bytes in 5 GiB (`5 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024`). Print `area = <value>`, `century seconds = <value>` and `bytes = <value>` on three lines. Print nothing else.

trap.class: INT32 wrap of literal-derived Ints (T1): a product of literals folds at 32 bits and prints a wrapped value with exit 0
trap.fix: W5 Core-0 widen on INT32 overflow (L0, 2026-10-07-1)

tasks.title: Parse large numeric IDs
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the numeric ID strings "42", "2147483647", "3000000000" and "9007199254740993" (Text, in that order; Aether's Int is 64-bit, so all of them fit). Convert each to an Int and print `<text> -> next <value + 1>`. Then print `sum = <sum of the four values>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: `parse_int` wraps past 2^31 (T1 family): "3000000000" parses as -1294967296, exit 0

tasks.title: Single-bit masks up to bit 40 via a helper
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a helper `bit(k: Int) -> Int` that returns the Int with only bit k set (2 to the power k; Aether's Int is 64-bit). Print `bit <k> = <bit(k)>` for k = 0, 10, 31, 32, 40 in that order, then `all = <the bitwise OR of those five masks>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: `<<` on a literal-derived Int works in 32 bits (part2 open list; L0's widening covers arithmetic, not shifts): `bit(32)` and `bit(40)` called with literals return 0, exit 0
trap.review: part2 open silent-wrong list (`<<` in 32 bits)

tasks.title: One Game of Life step with neighbour counts
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that runs one step of Conway's Game of Life on this 6x6 grid (row 0 first; `#` alive, `.` dead), with cells outside the grid counted as dead:

```
......
..#...
...#..
.###..
......
......
```

For each cell count its live neighbours among the 8 surrounding cells (the cell itself is not a neighbour). A live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours stays alive; a dead cell with exactly 3 becomes alive; every other cell is dead in the next generation. First print the neighbour counts of the ORIGINAL grid, one row per line, as the six digits with no separators. Then print the next generation as six lines of `#` and `.`. Finally print `alive = <number of live cells in the next generation>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: a nested `continue` (skip the centre cell) advanced every enclosing range counter (R1): the 8-neighbour loop counts wrong with exit 0

tasks.title: Pop every element of a stack
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that builds a stack as an `Int[]` (top at the end) by pushing 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 in that order and prints `size = <n>`. Then pop exactly as many times as the stack held elements when popping began: each pop removes the top element and prints `pop <value>`. Finally print `left = <number of elements remaining>`. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
size = 6
pop 60
pop 50
pop 40
pop 30
pop 20
pop 10
left = 0

trap.class: a range loop re-reads its bound every iteration (R2): `loop i in 0..length(stack)` while popping stops halfway, exit 0
trap.review: R2 / B-runtime-semantics-2 (the bug that corrupted algo_sliding_window_max)

tasks.title: Copy a grid and zero the copy's diagonal
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that builds a 4x4 `Int[][]` grid row by row with `grid[r][c] = r * 4 + c + 1`. Make an independent copy of the grid, then set every cell on the main diagonal (`r == c`) of the COPY to 0, leaving the original unchanged. Print `original row <r> sum = <s>` for r = 0..3, then `copy row <r> sum = <s>` for r = 0..3, then `original diagonal = <a b c d>` (the original's four diagonal values separated by single spaces). Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
original row 0 sum = 10
original row 1 sum = 26
original row 2 sum = 42
original row 3 sum = 58
copy row 0 sum = 9
copy row 1 sum = 20
copy row 2 sum = 31
copy row 3 sum = 42
original diagonal = 1 6 11 16

trap.class: 2-D array value semantics depend on how rows were built (R3): `let copy: Int[][] = grid;` shares loop-built rows, so zeroing the copy zeroes the original, exit 0

tasks.title: Shortest path in a maze (BFS with a Point record)
tasks.prompt:
Write an Aether program that finds the shortest path length in this 5x5 maze (row 0 first; `.` open, `#` wall), moving one step up, down, left or right between open cells:

```
..#..
.##.#
.....
#.#.#
...#.
```

Represent positions with `type Point { r: Int = 0; c: Int = 0; }`. Run a breadth-first search from the start (row 0, column 0). For each goal in order -- (2, 4), (4, 0), (4, 4) -- print `steps to (<r>,<c>) = <n>`, where `<n>` is the number of moves on a shortest path, or `-1` if the goal cannot be reached. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
steps to (2,4) = 6
steps to (4,0) = 6
steps to (4,4) = -1

trap.class: record `==` compares identity (T5): `if cur == goal` on two Points with equal fields is false, so every goal reads unreachable, exit 0

tasks.title: Greeting with a constant app name
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that declares the constant `const Name: Text = "Aether";` and a function `greet(name: Text) -> Text` that returns `Hello, <name>! Welcome to <Name>.`, where `<name>` is the argument and `<Name>` is the constant's value. Print `greet("Ada")` and then `greet("Linus")`, one per line. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Hello, Ada! Welcome to Aether.
Hello, Linus! Welcome to Aether.

trap.class: value names ignore case, so parameter `name` shadows `const Name` inside greet: `Welcome to Ada.`, exit 0
trap.review: part1: names ignore case (F6, F110); `fn check(limit) { ret LIMIT; }` returns the argument

tasks.title: Letter grades
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a function `grade(score: Int) -> Text` that returns `A` for a score of 90 or more, `B` for 80-89, `C` for 70-79 and `F` below 70. For each score in 95, 83, 71, 40 (in that order) print `<score>: <grade>`. Then print `passing = <number of those scores whose grade is not F>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: an if/else-if chain used as the function's tail expression (Rust style) is a discarded statement (G1): the function returns nil; printed directly it shows `nil` with exit 0, stored into a typed let it is an uncoded runtime error
trap.review: G1 (`grade(...)` with a tail if-chain gives `grade=nil`)

tasks.title: Clamp percentages with an early return
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a function `clampPct(x: Int) -> Int` that returns 0 for a negative `x`, 100 for an `x` above 100, and `x` itself otherwise. For each value in -5, 42, 100, 250 (in that order) print `clampPct(<x>) = <result>`. Then print `unchanged = <number of values whose result equals the value itself>`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: a bare tail expression after early `ret`s (`... ret 100; } x }`) passes FLOW-001 and returns nil on the fall-through path (G1 / FLOW-001 gap); printed directly it shows `nil` with exit 0, stored into a typed let it is an uncoded runtime error
trap.review: G1; *FLOW-001 misses a missing final ret*

tasks.title: Global lookup table of squares
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that keeps a global lookup table `squares: Int[]` holding `i * i` for i = 0..9, filled in once before any lookup. `main` then prints `squares[3] = <v>`, `squares[9] = <v>` and `table size = <length of the table>`, one per line. Print nothing else.

trap.class: a top-level statement other than `let` next to `fn main` (here the loop that fills the table) means main never runs (X3 / entry-point rule): no output, exit 0
trap.review: part1 entry-point rule (F71, F85, F91); part2 X3

tasks.title: Tag counts with an optional tags array
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `projects.json` is in the working directory, shaped `{"projects": [{"name": Text, "tags": [Text, ...]}, ...]}`. The `tags` key is optional: a project without it has zero tags. Write an Aether program that parses the file and, for each project in order, prints `<name>: <count> tags` where `<count>` is the number of entries in its `tags` array (0 when `tags` is absent). Then print `total tags = <sum of the counts>` and `untagged = <number of projects whose count is 0>`. Close the document. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
atlas: 3 tags
borealis: 0 tags
cirrus: 0 tags
delta: 1 tags
ember: 0 tags
total tags = 4
untagged = 3

trap.class: toon_len of an absent toon_key is -1, not the 0 the guides promise (NEST-001), so counts and totals go wrong silently
trap.fix: W5 runtime: an unused handle's length is 0

tasks.title: Uppercase every word
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the sentence `the quick brown fox` (lowercase ASCII words separated by single spaces). Print each word converted to uppercase on its own line, in order, and then print the whole sentence converted to uppercase on one more line. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
THE
QUICK
BROWN
FOX
THE QUICK BROWN FOX

trap.class: `upcase(word)` is Pascal's one-character UpCase: it returns only the first letter, exit 0

tasks.title: Right-aligned name column
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for the players "ada" (score 91), "grace" (score 78) and "linus" (score 85), held in arrays. Print one line per player, in that order: the name right-aligned in a field 8 characters wide (padded on the left with spaces), then ` | `, then the score. For example the first line is `     ada | 91`. Print nothing else.

trap.class: Pascal width specs on Text (R7): `name:8` on a computed or array-held Text prints `       ?` (a literal prints correctly), exit 0
trap.fix: shared BE FORMAT_VALUE for unicode strings (open)

tasks.title: Validate ports and exit with status 2
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that validates the port values "8080", "443", "80x", "22" (Text, in that order) with a helper `parsePort(t: Text) -> Int`. A valid port is a non-empty string of decimal digits. For each value in order: if it is valid print `port <value>`; if it is not, print `error: bad port <text>` and immediately end the whole program with exit status 2, so nothing after it runs and nothing more is printed. (Exiting with a status is `exit(n)` or `halt(n)` inside `fx`.) The program's exit status is graded as well as its output.

trap.class: `exit(n)` was Pascal's Exit(value) (R4): inside a non-Void helper it returns n from the helper, so the program prints `port 2`, carries on, and exits 0

tasks.title: Filter stdin records until end of input
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that reads standard input line by line until the end of input. Each line is `<name> <qty>` (a word, one space, a non-negative integer). For every line whose quantity is greater than 0 print `<name>: <qty>`, in input order. After the input is exhausted print `lines = <number of lines read>`, `kept = <number of lines printed>` and `total = <sum of all quantities>`, each on its own line. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
apple: 3
banana: 12
date: 7
fig: 21
lines = 6
kept = 4
total = 43
tasks.stdin:
apple 3
banana 12
cherry 0
date 7
elder 0
fig 21

trap.class: stdin (R6): `eof()` with no argument is always true, so a read-until-EOF loop processes 0 lines; on 2026-10-06-1 every console `readln` also writes ESC[?25h into stdout
